CSS Unveils Revitalized Brand, Reflecting Its Evolution as a Comprehensive Senior Living Technology Partner

CSS Unveils Revitalized Brand, Reflecting Its Evolution as a Comprehensive Senior Living Technology Partner

PR Newswire

PASADENA, Calif., Sept. 15, 2026

Refreshed identity reflects CSS's continued growth and expanded commitment to delivering technology solutions for senior living communities nationwide

PASADENA, Calif., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CSS today unveiled a revitalized brand that reflects the company's evolution, expanded capabilities, and growing role as a comprehensive technology partner for senior living communities.

Built around the new brand promise, "Confidence. Connections. Communities.", the refreshed identity was developed by the global branding firm, BrandingBusiness, and represents the rich legacy of CSS while clarifying the future brand positioning and business focus.

For more than 15 years, CSS has built its reputation serving senior living through DIRECTV and a commitment to responsive, accountable service. Today, CSS delivers Technology Solutions for Senior Living Communities across four critical areas: DIRECTV In-Room Entertainment; Wi-Fi, Internet & Business Communications (VoIP); Managed IT & Cyber Protection; and Modern Nurse Call Solutions.

"Senior living has never been about technology for us. It's about a caregiver who has one less thing to fight with at the start of a double shift, and a resident who can find her favorite program without having to ask for help," said Dave Saenz, Co-Founder & CEO of CSS. "Every community we serve is home to real people with real routines, and the TV in that room is often their window to the world. When we take the technology headaches off the plates of caregivers and administrators, we give them back time for the people they came to care for. That is the impact we want CSS to have, one community, one caregiver, and one resident at a time."

As senior living operators navigate rising technology costs, aging infrastructure, staffing challenges and an increasingly complex mix of vendors, CSS is expanding its role as "A partner who understands your world." The company's broader capabilities give communities one accountable technology partner and one point of contact across the critical systems they depend on every day.

"This is an exciting next chapter for CSS," said Markk Gonzales, Co-Founder & President of CSS. "We've listened to our customers, continued to invest in the senior living industry, and built our company around solving more of the challenges they face every day. Our new brand reflects the company we've become and, more importantly, our commitment to where we're going together with our customers."

The refreshed brand brings CSS's expanded capabilities and long-standing service philosophy together under one vision: "Confidence & connections for senior living communities." The goal is simple: make technology easier so senior living teams can stay focused on what matters most, the people in their care.

ABOUT CSS

CSS delivers Technology Solutions for Senior Living Communities, including DIRECTV entertainment, Wi-Fi and internet, business communications (VoIP), managed IT and cybersecurity, and modern nurse call solutions. With more than 15 years of senior living experience, CSS brings critical technologies together through one accountable partner focused on simplifying operations, improving efficiency and creating better resident experiences.

data.title: Wells Fargo just cut its S&P 500 price target. Will others follow?
data.description:
By Steve Goldstein

It's one of the first major Wall Street institutions to lower its expectations for stock-market performance since the spring

Wells Fargo strategists lowered their S&P 500 target.

In what may be a first since the early days of the war between the U.S. and Iran, a Wall Street firm is lowering rather than raising its S&P 500 year-end target.

Wells Fargo on Tuesday reduced its S&P 500 target to 7,700 from 7,950, after the index SPX closed Monday just below 7,620, up 11% on the year.

So-called top-down strategist forecasts are not as extensively tracked as Wall Street price targets on individual companies.

Strategists led by Ohsung Kwon said the downgrade comes even as the firm is growing more optimistic on earnings per share - targeting $425 next year for S&P 500 companies and $460 in 2028.

That's very optimistic. In a separate note, Bank of America analysts said the top-down consensus by strategists for 2027 EPS was $392. The so-called bottom-up projection - that is, adding up all the estimates of S&P 500 companies and then weighting by market cap - is $417.

However, the Wells Fargo team said the market is "entering late innings of the cycle, arguing for multiple compression." That refers to the multiple investors assign to each dollar of earnings. While they are not worried about 2027 EPS, they expressed concerns that AI capital expenditure would slow, eating into 2028 earnings.

Wells Fargo says 2027 EPS estimates look extreme.

Wells Fargo argued that 2027 earnings will be "cyclically elevated by 42%" compared with the trendline of what S&P 500 earnings should be at this stage of the economic cycle. The gap of 42% is the highest since the 1950s, they said.

By sector, Wells Fargo is lowering tech to equal-weight from overweight while raising healthcare to overweight from equal-weight. Within tech, Wells Fargo said it prefers software to microchips.

Tech stocks XLK have jumped 28% this year, while healthcare XLV has climbed 9%.

"We see the midterms as a potential risk to tech, especially as political pushback against data centers continues to gain momentum," the firm said.

A potential Democratic sweep would be seen as a positive for healthcare, potentially setting the stage for a restoration of the enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies, the firm added.

Earlier this week, Bank of America increased its year-end target, albeit to levels still below Wells Fargo's new target. BofA sees the index ending at 7,400 - versus 7,100 previously - as it launched a 12-month target of 7,800.

-Steve Goldstein

data.title: Bitcoin Falls Ahead of Senate Crypto Vote, Fed Decision
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid 




  Bitcoin fell Tuesday ahead of a Senate procedural vote on the Clarity Act, with investors looking to Washington for a potential catalyst after the cryptocurrency's August rally lost steam. 



  In early afternoon trading in Europe, bitcoin was trading down 2.8% at around $76,921, according to LSEG. 



  The Senate is scheduled to vote at around 2:15 p.m. ET on whether to advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, which aims to establish a regulatory framework for digital assets, including rules governing their issuance, trading and regulation. It needs Democratic support to secure the 60 votes required to clear the procedural hurdle. 



  The vote is the legislation's most immediate obstacle, said Andrew Melville, head of research at institutional crypto derivatives data and analytics firm Block Scholes. Even if it clears Tuesday's vote, the Senate version contains significant revisions from the legislation passed by the House and the differences would have to be reconciled before President Trump can sign it. 



  The bill's progress has been held up by disagreements over issues including consumer protection and restrictions on public officials profiting from crypto. Senate Banking Committee Democrats have continued to raise objections to the legislation's investor-protection and ethics provisions. 



   Prediction-market traders remain skeptical that the legislation will make it across the finish line this year. Polymarket puts the probability of the Clarity Act becoming law in 2026 at 19%, down from 31% Monday. Separately, traders give bitcoin a 72% chance of ending Tuesday between $76,000 and $78,000. 



  Polymarket has a data sharing partnership with Dow Jones, publisher of Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal. 



  Bitcoin rose around 25% between Aug. 19 and Aug. 25 and climbed above $82,000 at the start of September before pulling back. Investors have recently viewed $80,000 as an opportunity to sell, said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares. 



  Investors are also awaiting the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision Wednesday. Analysts have pointed to both progress on crypto regulation and the Fed decision as potential catalysts for bitcoin as it struggles to regain the $80,000 level.

data.title: College Without the Debt: How National Heritage Academies Students Are Earning a $67,000 College Degree for Free
data.description:
College Without the Debt: How National Heritage Academies Students Are Earning a $67,000 College Degree for Free

College Without the Debt: How National Heritage Academies Students Are Earning a $67,000 College Degree for Free

PR Newswire

GRAND RAPIDS, Mich., Sept. 15, 2026

Early College students can earn an associate degree while still in high school, potentially saving families tens of thousands of dollars.

GRAND RAPIDS, Mich., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- "I couldn't imagine how much money worth of free education my kids have received through this program."

For Ciara Selden-Ruffin, the mother of Grand River Preparatory High School Early College student Aamir Hollowell, the financial impact of the Early College program has been substantial. It has given Aamir the opportunity to earn an associate degree without the family taking on the tuition bill.

That kind of financial head start is critical for families worrying about how they will pay for college.

The nation's federal student loan portfolio stands at nearly $1.7 trillion, with about 44.6 million borrowers carrying federal education debt. The issue is back in the national spotlight as changes to the Saving on a Valuable Education, or SAVE, Plan ended, requiring millions of borrowers to find a new way to repay their federal student loans.

For families with children approaching college, the uncertainty underscores a different question: What if students could reduce or even avoid some college debt before graduating from high school?

National Heritage Academies® (NHA®) Early College program is helping their students do exactly that.

A $67,000 Head Start

At Grand River Prep, an NHA partner-school in Grand Rapids, Mich., students can earn college credits, career credentials, and even an associate degree through the school's Early College partnership with Davenport University.

Tuition, fees, and books are covered through the program. Based on Davenport's current published undergraduate tuition rate, the value of a two-year associate degree can total approximately $67,000.

Felicia Pope, who works with Davenport University's Early College partnerships, said the program can put students in a very different financial position when they enter adulthood.

"You can be 18, 19 years old, you have an associate degree, you have the entry-level position in the field, without any student loans," Pope said.

Students can use that degree to begin working in their chosen field or continue toward a bachelor's degree with a significant amount of college coursework already completed. "You're halfway through your degree, saved a ton of time, a ton of money," Pope said.

Nine of NHA's high schools have an Early College program. During the 2024-25 school year, 565 students earned 5,186 college credits, saving an estimated $1.12 million in college tuition.

For NHA, the opportunity is about making college more accessible while preparing students for what comes next.

Koree Woodward, NHA Director of High Schools, says Early College is a natural extension of NHA's mission to prepare students for life after graduation.

"The program makes college feel more attainable for families who may not have otherwise seen it as an accessible option," Woodward said. "It helps students develop the knowledge, habits, character, and sense of responsibility needed for lifelong learning, college success, and meaningful careers."

College With a Support System

The financial savings are only part of the Early College model.

Students gradually transition into college-level work, beginning with one college course per semester during 10th grade before increasing their coursework in their junior and senior years.

Pope calls it a "soft launch into college."

Davenport advisors work directly with students on applications, degree pathways, scheduling, and course selection. Grand River Prep advisors provide another layer of support, helping students monitor grades, manage college expectations, and stay on track.

Aamir Hollowell sees that support firsthand.

"Every week, you have a meeting with your advisor to help you stay on track," she said. "They just keep checking up on you."

Grand River Prep Early College Advisor Jayme McWain said students get the independence of college without having to navigate the experience alone.

"For them to have kind of a safety net and a support system built in is a really great feature of that program," McWain said. "It creates so much more access and skill building."

From College Credit to Career

In addition to the tuition savings, students can leave high school with college experience, career opportunities, and potentially two years of college already completed.

For some students, that head start can translate directly into a career.

Grand River Prep graduate Kennah Kalele earned an associate degree in medical assisting through Early College and is now pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Nursing at Grand Valley State University.

"I don't have to take any gen eds in the college that I'm going to, and I'm even ahead in some aspects of my nursing degree," Kalele said.

Her associate degree also helped her begin gaining professional experience. Kalele works part time as a medical transport technician while continuing her education.

For McWain, the value is clear.

"Anytime you can help someone get free college when the price is off the charts, that's a great thing," she said.

And for families like Ciara Selden-Ruffin's, it offers the opportunity for her children to start their futures with a college education rather than a tuition bill.

About National Heritage Academies:

National Heritage Academies® (NHA®) was founded in 1995 with families in mind and the belief that every child deserves an education that builds knowledge and character. Today, NHA supports 105 tuition-free, partner-schools across nine states, serving more than 65,000 K-12 students through rigorous academics and Moral Focus™ programming. NHA

data.title: Supreme Twins Foundation Gala Raises Critical Support for Special Needs Children, Young Adults, and Families
data.description:
Supreme Twins Foundation Gala Raises Critical Support for Special Needs Children, Young Adults, and Families

Supreme Twins Foundation Gala Raises Critical Support for Special Needs Children, Young Adults, and Families

PR Newswire

MIAMI, Sept. 15, 2026

Celebrity designer Giannina Azar and Latin Grammy winners Tony Succar and Albita headline an inspirational evening supporting neurodivergent youth  

MIAMI, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Born from a family's personal journey raising twin daughters with special needs, the Supreme Twins Foundation brought together nearly 400 South Florida civic, business, and philanthropic leaders at the JW Marriott Marquis Miami for its 2nd Annual Gala and Fashion Showcase. While the evening featured high fashion and award-winning performances, the heart of the event focused on expanding educational and developmental support for youth with disabilities as they transition into adulthood. 

The gala secured vital funding for the Foundation's core initiatives: PAP, which helps families access essential psychological assessments and other resources required by insurers; Artistic Expression, featuring student art and music programming; and Special Continuing Education, supporting partnerships like Miami Dade College's ACCESS Program and EmpowerU Summer Camp to offer neurodivergent youth education, vocational training, and life skills for greater independence and self-sufficiency.

The event featured over 30 couture designs by Dominican-Lebanese designer Giannina Azar, whose creations have dressed stars like Beyoncé and Jennifer Lopez, alongside live performances by Latin Grammy winners Tony Succar and Albita Rodríguez, and a special showcase by students from the Foundation's music program.  

Yet, between the fashion showcase and musical sets, the evening remained centered on family impact. Co-founders Ilieva and Miguel Valdés established the Foundation after navigating care for their twin daughters, Nathaly and Nicolee, diagnosed with Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS). 

"This foundation was born out of love and the determination to build a better future for our daughters," said Ilieva Valdés, co-founder of the Supreme Twins Foundation. "When our twin girls were diagnosed, we realized how overwhelming this journey is for parents. Tonight is about showing these families that they are not alone."

Among its various efforts, the Foundation also assists youth navigating the transition out of traditional school support systems at age 22, when families face an abrupt drop-off in daily care and therapies.

"Seeing our community come together proves that when we invest in these children and young adults, we enrich everyone," added co-founder Miguel Valdés. "Turning 22 shouldn't mean the end. It should be the beginning of a new chapter."

Learn more at www.supremetwins.org.

Aardvark Therapeutics (AARD) Investors: Securities Fraud Class Action Filed, Contact Hagens Berman Before October 13, 2026 Lead Plaintiff Deadline

Aardvark Therapeutics (AARD) Investors: Securities Fraud Class Action Filed, Contact Hagens Berman Before October 13, 2026 Lead Plaintiff Deadline

PR Newswire

SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 15, 2026

SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hagens Berman Sobol Shapiro LLP, a national shareholder rights firm, notifies investors in Aardvark Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: AARD) of a pending securities class action lawsuit.

Investors who purchased or acquired Aardvark common stock pursuant and/or traceable to the offering documents issued in connection with the Company's initial public offering (IPO) on or about February 13, 2025, and/or purchased or acquired Aardvark securities between February 13, 2025 and May 14, 2026 (the Class Period), are encouraged to contact our firm now.

Watch our video on the Aardvark investigation: youtu.be/pY5E36QoCqo

Key Case Details & Important Deadlines

  • Lead Plaintiff Motion Deadline: October 13, 2026 
  • Visit: www.hbsslaw.com/aard 
  • Contact the Firm Now: AARD@hbsslaw.com 
                                           844-916-0895

What is the Lawsuit About?

The complaint alleges that Aardvark Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing small-molecule therapies targeting bitter taste receptors (TAS2Rs) such as ARD-101 for the treatment of hyperphagia in Prader-Willi Syndrome (PWS), made materially false and misleading statements and/or failed to disclose critical information.

Specifically, the action points out that the offering documents and defendants failed to disclose:

  1. That ARD-101 was significantly less safe than defendants had led investors to believe;
  2. That unexpected, reversible cardiac observations (such as QRS prolongation) occurred during trials at above-target doses; and
  3. Consequently, Aardvark's clinical, regulatory, and commercial prospects—including the Phase 3 Hunger Elimination or Reduction Objective (HERO) trial and open-label extension (OLE)—were materially overstated.

The Truth Emerges: Voluntarily Pause and FDA Clinical Hold

  • February 27, 2026: Aardvark announced it was voluntarily pausing its Phase 3 HERO trial due to "reversible cardiac observations at above target therapeutic doses found during routine safety monitoring in a healthy volunteer study." Following this news, Aardvark's stock price plummeted over 56%. 
  • May 14, 2026:  Aardvark announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) placed a full clinical hold on its investigational new drug application (IND) for ARD-101, halting all ongoing studies under the IND, including the Phase 3 HERO trial and OLE trial. Aardvark's stock price fell another 32.1%.

Hagens Berman's Investigation

"We're investigating the suit's allegations, including that Aardvark allegedly misled investors about ARD-101's development, its safety and efficacy," said Reed Kathrein, the Hagens Berman partner leading the firm's investigation of the claims in the pending suit.

What Can Aardvark Investors Do?

If you are a class member who suffered losses on Aardvark securities, you have until October 13, 2026, to ask the Court to appoint you as Lead Plaintiff for the class.  The firm welcomes AARD investors to contact the firm to discuss their legal rights and potential recovery options.

If you'd like more information and answers to frequently asked questions about the firm's Aardvark investigation, read more »

Whistleblowers: Persons with non-public information regarding Aardvark Therapeutics should consider their options to help in the investigation or take advantage of the SEC Whistleblower program. Under the new program, whistleblowers who provide original information may receive rewards totaling up to 30 percent of any successful recovery made by the SEC. For more information, call Reed Kathrein at 844-916-0895 or email AARD@hbsslaw.com.

Hagens Berman is a global plaintiffs' rights complex litigation firm focusing on corporate accountability. The firm is home to a robust practice and represents investors as well as whistleblowers, workers, consumers and others in cases achieving real results for those harmed by corporate negligence and other wrongdoings. data.title: Oomph and Adapt USA Combine Forces to Become Pare & Co
data.description:
Oomph and Adapt USA Combine Forces to Become Pare & Co

New brand reflects the evolution of the nearly 20-year-old digital consultancy and its expansion for the AI era

Oomph today announced the launch of Pare & Co (Pare), a new name and brand that reflects how the digital consultancy has evolved over nearly two decades, including its recent acquisition of Adapt USA and its growing investment in AI.

Founded in Providence in 2007, Oomph began with a focus on smaller-scale digital work where, as the name suggested, a little extra “oomph” could make the difference between something good and something great.

Today, the scale and complexity of the work are very different. Tens of millions of people depend on the websites, platforms, and digital products Pare creates with its clients. Pare works with organizations across healthcare, financial services, technology and other complex industries, including Brown University Health, Workhuman, nCino and 8am. In these sectors, digital experiences have to do more than work well. They have to be accurate, accessible, secure, and worthy of people's trust.

Pare brings Oomph and Adapt USA together under a single brand and a new model for digital consulting organized around outcomes rather than deliverables. Every engagement begins by identifying the outcome that matters most: Trust, Engagement, Growth, or Intelligence. Senior people own the judgment and the outcome, bringing together the capabilities and expertise needed to move it.

“Pare is the perfect combination for Adapt's present and future customers. With our expanded services and new brand, our customers will be delighted,” said Doug Sisko, Managing Director of Pare’s Growth Practice and founder of Adapt USA.

“This is such an exciting time in technology. Organizations are being asked to move faster and successful adoption of AI is making that a reality. But, the clients we serve can't afford to trade speed for trust, accuracy, security or reliability,” said Christopher Murray, founder and CEO of Pare. “The opportunity isn't simply to do the same work faster. It's to rethink what we can do for our clients and how we do it.”

Pare brings Oomph and Adapt USA together under a single brand and a broader model for digital consulting. The firm combines senior strategic judgment with AI-enabled delivery to help clients understand the problem that matters most, determine what should be done, and bring together the right expertise to do it.

The name Pare reflects that approach. “Operating at this level requires business understanding, strategic thinking and the ability to navigate a great deal of complexity,” Mathew O’Bryant, President of Pare, said. “Pare means getting through that complexity to the core of the problem so we can move forward with what matters most.”

The launch includes a new visual identity, website, and an expanded set of capabilities spanning strategy, experience design, technology, digital growth, and intelligence.

For existing Oomph and Adapt clients, the transition to Pare doesn’t change their current work or teams. It simply marks the next stage of a transformation that has been underway inside the company for years.

About Pare & Co

Pare & Co is an AI-native digital consultancy that helps organizations navigate complexity with confidence. The firm combines senior strategic judgment with human and agentic delivery to create websites, platforms, products and the intelligence inside them. Pare works with organizations where complexity is high and the cost of error is higher, focusing every engagement on the outcome that matters most: Trust, Engagement, Growth or Intelligence. Learn more at http://pare.co or email hello@pare.co
